body:
We should see about improving how agents are told by solace to respond in discussions. An agent tried to respond to a discussion this way and it failed, sending "--text "### What I'm suggesting" to the discussion instead:

solace task note --text "### What I'm suggesting The code is right as it stands; the review found only two wording problems in the docs. I rechecked the files after the review (the project changed during it), and both are still present. **1. `solace-cli/README.md:16` — the inaccurate bullet.** It says `build.rs` \"runs each project's `build-release` command\", which implies `migration` has one. It does not: `solace-cli/migration/solace.toml` declares only `migration-tests` and `migration-browser`. The migration client reaches the binary inside the frontend bundle, via the frontend's `migration = { path = \"../migration\" }`. Current: ``` - `board/`, `frontend/`, `migration/`: the web clients, bundled into the binary by `build.rs`, which runs each project's `build-release` command. ``` Suggested: ``` - `board/`, `frontend/`, `migration/`: the web clients, bundled into the binary by `build.rs`, which runs the `build-release` command in `board` and `frontend`; the migration client is bundled as part of the frontend bundle. ``` **2. `frontend/README.md` — a leftover sentence.** The Build section ends with \"Rebuild this bundle after changing either app\", which is the old two-app wording; the rebuild is now triggered by changes in three sources (frontend, board, migration), as the paragraph's first sentence already says. I suggest deleting the sentence, since the paragraph already states that `cargo build` rebuilds `priv/app.js` when any of the three changes. **3. `frontend/README.md` — a formatting nit.** In Server integration, the sentence about the board's fonts and `/guide` runs onto one long line, breaking the file's wrapping. I suggest rewrapping it to match the surrounding lines. ### Why this matters The README line is the one place that tells someone how to extend `build.rs`. If they add a third `build_release(&root.join(\"migration\"), &own)` to match \"each project\", the build script panics on `migration declares no [commands] build-release run`. Naming the two projects in the prose keeps the docs and `main()` in the same shape. ### Verification so far - `build --project solace-cli/frontend`: passed; `check --project solace-cli/frontend`: no errors, 0 warnings; `test --all --project solace-cli/frontend`: 3/3. - `run cargo-timings --project .`: passed — the build script ran both `build-release` commands (board 0.31 MB, frontend 0.30 MB) and emitted the `rerun-if-changed` lines for both projects plus `board/src`, `board/gleam.toml`, `migration/src`, `migration/gleam.toml`. - `run rust-acceptance --project .`: passed, 4 suites (board 28, view 2, workspace 12, migrate 20), including `test_a11_embedded_client_and_internal_files`, which checks `/app.js` contains `/workflow`. - `run rust-board-tests --project .`: passed, 15 unit tests. ### Question Do you want me to write these three doc fixes? `solace-cli/README.md` is in project `.` and `frontend/README.md` is in `solace-cli/frontend`, both within this task's reach, so I can propose both writes for your approval. " --project solace-cli/frontend
title: Improve agent's info about discussion
